title: Canada-resident NRI trapped using a fake ID, demand of 50 thousand dollars, Ghaziabad police's big action against a sextortion gang

reading.body:
This is an impersonation case. A fake Facebook profile was used to make contact, and the harm began with a person being induced into a compromising video call under a false identity. The AI element sits at the threat stage: police said the gang threatened to circulate AI-generated obscene videos alongside the recorded footage. The system was not deployed to deceive a decision-maker or to answer a query, it was used to manufacture blackmail material about a real person.

The failure was not caught at any point in the contact chain. A platform hosting a fake profile had no check that surfaced it before the victim engaged. The extortion demand and the AI-generated videos were the first points at which the deception became visible to the target, and by then the leverage already existed. Catching this earlier would have required identity verification at profile creation or detection of the generated media before it was used as a threat, neither of which the reporting shows happened.

What is not established is guilt. The arrests and the police account are allegations, and no trial outcome is reported. The link between the accused and the 130 bank accounts, and the claim that the gang was active since 2023, rest on police statements rather than on findings.

summary:
A Jamia Millia Islamia student named Md Faisal and three associates from Muzaffarnagar were arrested in Ghaziabad for allegedly extorting a Canada-based NRI. Police said the gang created a fake Facebook profile, contacted the victim on Messenger, recorded him in a compromising position during a video call on Sept 10, then demanded $50,000, about Rs 4.7 crore, while threatening to circulate the footage and AI-generated obscene videos. The victim reported the matter to the cybercrime team on Sept 17.

Police said the accused's mobile number was linked to 40 cyber fraud complaints on the NCRB portal, and an FIR was registered under the BNS and IT Act. Four gang members were arrested on Friday while some associates remain absconding. Investigators found AI sextortion videos on their phones and links to at least 130 bank accounts holding Rs 6.6 crore. Police said the gang had been active since 2023.
